title: Utro / Workload Resources
description: Per-service CPU and memory. Replicas of the same Deployment/StatefulSet/DaemonSet are aggregated into one series, so the view survives a rollout and is comparable over time.

panels.title: CPU usage by service
panels.description: CPU cores consumed, summed across all replicas of the workload. 1 core = 1 full CPU. A t3.medium node has 2 cores, so 0.5 here is a quarter of one node. Not a percentage — see 'CPU vs requests' for that.

panels.title: CPU vs requests
panels.description: Cores used as a percentage of the cores REQUESTED. 100% means the workload is using exactly what the scheduler reserved for it. Above 100% is not an error — CPU is compressible, so it is borrowing idle capacity it has no guarantee of keeping. Sustained above 100% means the request is set too low.

panels.title: CPU throttling by service
panels.description:
Percentage of time the workload spent throttled against its CPU LIMIT — 20% means one second in five was spent waiting for CPU it was not allowed to use. Anything sustained above zero means the limit is actively slowing the service.

EXPECTED TO BE EMPTY on this cluster: the underlying metric only exists for containers that set a CPU limit, and these workloads set requests only. No data here means 'no limits configured', not 'no throttling'.

panels.title: Memory usage by service
panels.description:
Memory in use, summed across all replicas of the workload.

This is the WORKING SET: memory the kernel cannot reclaim under pressure. It is deliberately not container_memory_usage_bytes, which includes reclaimable page cache and so overstates real usage. The working set is the number the OOM killer compares against the limit.

panels.title: Memory vs limits
panels.description:
Memory in use as a percentage of the memory LIMIT.

Unlike CPU, this is a hard ceiling — memory is not compressible, so reaching 100% is an OOMKill and a restart, not a slowdown. Treat sustained red as an imminent restart. Blank rows are workloads with no memory limit set, which cannot be OOMKilled by their own limit but can still be evicted under node pressure.

panels.title: Memory headroom before OOMKill
panels.description:
Bytes remaining before the memory limit is hit, per workload.

A series trending toward zero is heading for an OOMKill — this is the same information as 'Memory vs limits' but as an absolute amount, which is easier to reason about when sizing a limit.

Workloads with no memory limit set are absent from this panel by design: they have no ceiling to run out of.

panels.title: Container restarts by service
panels.description:
Container restarts, counted per graph interval rather than as a running total, so each spike is one restart event.

Line up a spike here with 'Memory headroom' to the left: a restart immediately after headroom reached zero is an OOMKill. A restart with headroom to spare is a crash or a failed probe instead.
